# Anomalies and the Land-Spirits

## What the troubles are

> status: ratified (D-0007, D-0008)

The world's sickness surfaces as many smaller animist problems — the yokai-episode
engine transplanted whole into pre-Christian Northern European soil. The troubles are
local, physical, and strange: a well that sours, a field the frost won't leave, a
thing in the treeline that used to be the river's good neighbor. They are symptoms.
The disease is upstream ([[wyrd-and-frith]]).

## Landvættir

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The land-wights of Norse tradition, adopted as the resident spirits of specific
places. They are not demons and not fae-courts: they are parties to old agreements —
chaotic-neutral, etiquette-bound, lethal when wronged. Most were quiet partners of
human life for centuries. The broken ones the story meets are creditors of debts no
one alive remembers signing, trying to balance a ledger with the only tools a river or
a hill has.

## Taxonomy and forensics

> status: provisional (D-0059, D-0072)

Spirits obey ecosystem logic — habitats, diets, seasons, structural weaknesses — and
every region's Wyrd expresses trouble differently, which is why each new territory is
a fresh education ([[regions]]). Facing an anomaly is forensic work: read the ground,
test the water, trace the treaty, find the contradiction. The investigation IS the
adventure; the "monster stats" are its history.

## Resolution without elimination

> status: ratified (D-0005, D-0006, D-0055)

You cannot stab a contradiction. Encounters resolve the Kishōtenketsu way — through a
perspective shift and reconciliation — with the climax being a spoken proof that
dissolves the false premise, restructures the broken agreement, and lets the land
settle. This is the feminist inversion of the battle formula: restoration over
elimination, precision over force. Violence exists in this world (the empire has
plenty), but it is never the mechanism by which an anomaly is truly ended.

## Beyond the monster hunt

> status: ratified (D-0105)

A standing requirement on all anomaly design: the ways logical disruption manifests
in the ecosystem must be developed with real nuance — never simplistic
monster-hunter tropes. A disruption might surface as weather, as behavior, as
absence, as wrongness in pattern — a creature is only one of many shapes, and the
least interesting default. This deepens D-0012 (no monster-of-the-week spine) from
structure into texture.

## The manifestation modes

> status: ratified (D-0105, D-0125)

Six modes by which a logical disruption surfaces, ordered subtlest to rarest, each with its
own audio treatment (this is an audio-first show):

1. **Seasonal / weather wrongness** — the calendar goes out of true: a frost that won't leave
   a field, a tide an hour early, fog pooling where it shouldn't. Played as the *wrong ambient
   bed* — a soundscape that contradicts the stated season, so the ear hears wrongness before
   anyone names it.
2. **Behavioural corruption** — creatures act against their nature (herd-beasts walking into
   the bog, a dog that won't cross a threshold), escalating to people caught in small wrong
   loops (a headman re-counting a finished tally, a geas-bound tradesman who cannot speak a
   true sentence). Played as *repetition that won't resolve* — the sound of compulsion.
3. **Pattern-wrongness and absence** — nothing dramatic, only a hole: the frogs go silent, a
   well stops echoing, a day's road now takes two. Played as *subtraction* — an expected ambient layer
   drops out; the Frieren courage-to-hold-silence mode, and the most audio-native.
4. **Slow material rot** — the debt sours matter itself: iron that rusts overnight, chalk
   blackening, springwater gone copper, keep-stamped tools failing faster. Played as *texture
   foley* — wrongness heard in ordinary handling sounds.
5. **Spatial / temporal seams** — the land's capacity to hold consequence fractures: a
   fog-valley that eats short-term memory, a corridor where a proof won't hold, a circle
   running hot that bends the paths around it. Played as *disorientation*, used sparingly.
6. **The embodied creature (rare endpoint)** — only at the far end of accumulated debt does a
   trouble take a shape one can face: a broken river-landvættir risen as a wounded titan, a
   Wyrd-beast, a proof-gone-malignant monster (debugging, not hunting — monsters are not
   animals). Because the earlier five modes trained the ear on subtler wrongness, the
   creature-foley lands hard and stays rare, never routine (D-0012).

A single trouble usually escalates *through* several modes as its debt accumulates, and the
adventure is reading the mode and tracing it upstream to its human, systemic cause, then
dissolving the false premise with a proof so the land settles ("resolution without
elimination", above). Liminal people ([[human-variance]], D-0118) are the human reading on
this same gauge — a person lightly debt-written is mode 4 wearing a face.

## Wonder amid ruin

> status: ratified (D-0025)

Per the Sanderson framing: the anomalies must carry awe, not just horror. A broken
river-spirit can be terrible and breathtaking at once. The listener should feel the
emotion of exploration — a pioneer's dread and delight — never a monster-manual grind.

### Proposed textures

> status: proposed

Session sketches never ruled on: "wounded titans" too vast to dispel, which
communities herd and soothe like natural disasters; spirits whose etiquette retains
old-fae rules (never thank them; a gift closes no debt); anomaly behavior keyed to the
soil itself (sulfur peat, chalk, iron clay producing different manifestations).
